newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 17.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The first of the cabinet's economic measures which Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced yesterday could go into effect tomorrow. This measure is an import deposit, which importers of food and consumer goods will have to make without interest for 180 days.
- The crown strengthened to 0.58 percent under parity yesterday as a result of the announcement of the contents of the package of economic measures.
- According to cabinet sources, Vice-chairman Josef Lux, a team for subduing economic and financial criminality should be established within one week.
- Retail sales in February decreased by 0.6 percent, a slight improvement over January's decline of 2.3 percent.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Slovak central bank called on the Czech National Bank this week not to prolong returning the Slovak gold which belonged to the former Czechoslovak federal bank.

- The compulsory administrator of Agrobanka announced that the minimum sale price of the bank will be around four billion crowns. This sum comes from the value of Agrobanka's sound credits, confirmed by an audit.

- Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB) had net profit last year of 882 million crowns according to international accounting standards, and 857 million according to Czech accounting methods, which factor into the decision in the payment of dividends.

PRAVO - The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) and the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) are running even in the polls at 23 percent, according to a survey by IVVM. ODS lost three percentage points, and CSSD gained four.
- The cabinet should approve the choice of Western supersonic fighter aircrafts for the army by the end of this year, according to Deputy Defence Minister Vladimir Suman.
- The Vice-president of Harvard Group, Lubomir Puzej, said 16 Harvard funds should convert into open-end funds within the next two weeks.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The cabinet approved a new consumer and income tax law valid from January 1, 1998. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said the corporate tax rate will be decreased to 35 percent from 39 percent, while income taxes for physical persons will increase, as will consumer taxes on cigarettes, alcohol, petrol and motor oils.
- The financial group of Ceska Sporitelna had net profits in 1996 of 2.74 billion crowns, almost double its 1995 profits.
- The union federation is not pleased with the cabinet's plans to put the brakes on wage increases, and it is considering protests, demonstrations and even a general strike.
